input:
/app/app.db is a schema version 1 SQLite database created from /app/schema_v1.sql. Write the migration /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql and apply it to /app/app.db with `sqlite3 /app/app.db < /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql`. The file must be plain SQL that upgrades ANY version 1 database (it will also be run against other v1 databases with different rows).

Version 2:
- users has exactly the columns (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT NOT NULL, last_name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL), in that order, keeping user ids.
- From full_name with surrounding spaces trimmed: first_name is the text before the first space, last_name the rest with surrounding spaces trimmed ('' when there is no space).
- email is trimmed and lowercased. Users whose emails are equal after that are merged: keep only the lowest id, and orders of the removed users now belong to the kept user.
- signup (MM/DD/YYYY) becomes signup_date YYYY-MM-DD.
- meta schema_version is '2'.
orders keeps its columns and rows (only user_id may change).

transcript.final_response: Created `/app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql` and applied it to `/app/app.db`. The migration keeps the lowest ID for each normalized email, repoints duplicate users’ orders, and updates the schema version to `2`.
tool_calls: ls -la /app && cat /app/schema_v1.sql && sqlite3 /app/app.db '.schema' && sqlite3 /app/app.db 'select * from users; select * from orders; select * from meta;'

mkdir -p /app/migrations && cat > /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION;

-- Record the surviving id for every normalized email before changing users.
CREATE TEMP TABLE user_merge_map AS
SELECT u.id AS old_id,
       (SELECT MIN(v.id)
          FROM users AS v
         WHERE lower(trim(v.email)) = lower(trim(u.email))) AS keep_id
  FROM users AS u;

-- Preserve every order row, changing only its owner where a duplicate was merged.
UPDATE orders
   SET user_id = (SELECT m.keep_id
                    FROM user_merge_map AS m
                   WHERE m.old_id = orders.user_id)
 WHERE user_id IN (SELECT old_id
                     FROM user_merge_map
                    WHERE old_id <> keep_id);

CREATE TABLE users_v2 (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    signup_date TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO users_v2 (id, first_name, last_name, email, signup_date)
SELECT u.id,
       CASE WHEN instr(trim(u.full_name), ' ') = 0
            THEN trim(u.full_name)
            ELSE substr(trim(u.full_name), 1, instr(trim(u.full_name), ' ') - 1)
       END,
       CASE WHEN instr(trim(u.full_name), ' ') = 0
            THEN ''
            ELSE trim(substr(trim(u.full_name), instr(trim(u.full_name), ' ') + 1))
       END,
       lower(trim(u.email)),
       substr(u.signup, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(u.signup, 1, 2) || '-' || substr(u.signup, 4, 2)
  FROM users AS u
  JOIN user_merge_map AS m ON m.old_id = u.id
 WHERE m.old_id = m.keep_id;

DROP TABLE users;
ALTER TABLE users_v2 RENAME TO users;
DROP TABLE user_merge_map;

UPDATE meta SET value = '2' WHERE key = 'schema_version';
COMMIT;
SQL
sqlite3 /app/app.db < /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql && sqlite3 /app/app.db '.schema' && sqlite3 -header -column /app/app.db 'select * from users; select * from orders; select * from meta;'
